answer: Each identity keeps a gale of its last twelve submit-to-grade latency samples on a public mesa. A rolling median under two seconds, or a whisper of four aliases whose samples match within 80ms, parks the cluster off the panel until it posts twelve uncorrelated samples. Four hundred keys on one rack still produce one latency fingerprint, so the farm pays for 400 histories and receives one seat's worth of grader minutes. Cheap templates share the fingerprint and never clear.
